articles.title: Javier Milei's Case Against AI Regulation
articles.content:
"As much as the industrial revolution freed us from the constraints of the human muscle, AI will free us from the constraints of the human brain, pushing productivity beyond our wildest dreams….Keep AI unregulated so that it is free to be developed without the deadly hand of premature and poorly understood regulation."

Argentine President Javier Milei wrote that on June 4 in the Financial Times as part of his push to bring AI companies to Argentina. The prior week, he had introduced legislation to boost AI based on three pillars: leaving AI unregulated, establishing a new legal category for nonhuman corporations operated by AI agents or robots, and keeping corporate taxes low. As of late September, the Senate has held hearings on the legislation but not advanced it.

The post Javier Milei's Case Against AI Regulation appeared first on Reason Magazine.

articles.content:

articles.title: Brickbat: Don't Slap Me Five
articles.content:
Philip Morant School and College, a public secondary school in England, faced strong criticism after introducing a rule banning physical contact between students, including high-fives, hugs, and linking arms. The controversy grew after a student received detention for high-fiving a friend. School leaders say the rule was introduced after an increase in overly physical behavior disrupted classes. But many parents and students argue that it treats normal, friendly behavior as misconduct and prevents students from learning the difference between appropriate and inappropriate contact. A petition calls on the school to replace the blanket ban with rules that allow normal, consensual interactions while still addressing fighting, bullying, and unwanted touching. After receiving criticism, the school scrapped the policy.

The post Brickbat: Don't Slap Me Five appeared first on Reason Magazine.

articles.title: Vivek Ramaswamy, Elizabeth Holmes, and Jesus
articles.content:
If you enjoy Freed Up, come watch Robby debate at our upcoming Reason Versus in D.C. Tickets are available here.
On this week's episode of Freed Up, Robby Soave and Christian Britschgi condemn Vivek Ramaswamy's new attack ad against opponent Amy Acton before discussing their predictions for the 2026 midterm elections. Next, the boys get biblical with references to their favorite parables as they discuss Tyler Cowen's latest article on why he thinks Elizabeth Holmes—and most other non-violent female criminals—should not be in prison. The episode wraps with a thoughtful discussion on aging, state attorneys general, and the latest Meta settlement.
